title: Чужое парковочное место  (Someone Else's Parking Spot)

segments.t: Out in the courtyard, a parking attendant tells Chef Barinov that his usual spot is taken because an important guest paid extra to park there. Eager to stand up for his boss, Max marches over to tell the driver off, only to realize too late that he has just insulted a powerful friend of the restaurant.
Извините, но в данный момент ваше место занято.
Между прочим, это он занял ваше место.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
Извините, но в данный момент ваше место занято.
'Excuse me, but at the moment your parking spot is taken.' Barinov cuts in openly beside Max, refusing to let the moment slip past.
'You knew it was mine.' Max counters lightly beside Barinov, making his position completely clear.
'And for how many years now.' Barinov follows up frankly during the talk and uses "uzhe" ("already, now") to carry the main weight of the thought.
'In short.' Turning calmly before Barinov, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'I understand, everything is fine.' Barinov jumps in dryly with a sigh, leaving no doubt about where he stands.
'A man drove up and paid for it.' Max weighs in boldly at once and chooses "zaplatil" ("to pay", from the root "zaplatit") so Barinov hears the exact meaning.
'What an unexpected meeting.' Focusing on an unexpected meeting in this beat, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'And what are you doing here?' Max challenges skeptically before Barinov can change the subject.
Между прочим, это он занял ваше место.
'By the way, he is the one who took your spot.' Underscoring the place in front of Max, Barinov brings in "mesto" ("place, post") to make the meaning unmistakable.
'Chef, I have a counter-proposal.' Max counters earnestly facing Barinov, watching Barinov's face to see how the news lands.
'I will handle it myself, Chef.' Max counters pointedly with a smile, steering the talk right where he wants it.
'Damn, I screwed up again.' Focusing on the darn right here, Max brings in "lazhanulsya" ("to screw up", from "lazhanutsya") as the key Russian word here.
'How was I supposed to know?' Holding firm dryly around Max, Barinov puts the question word "otkuda" right at the start so Max hears the focus immediately.
Извините, но в данный момент ваше место занято.
Между прочим, это он занял ваше место.
That wraps up this scene as max tries to defend Chef Barinov's parking spot in the courtyard, only to accidentally insult the restaurant's wealthy VIP guest and embarrass the Chef. See you next time!
